backlog.spec: Replace the equal-weight rank average with weights learned from the training data. Inside fit_predict, run a single 5-fold StratifiedKFold (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the training set to obtain out-of-fold class-1 probabilities for each of the three feature-set XGBoost members. Compute each member's out-of-fold AUROC a_i, convert to weights w_i = max(a_i - 0.5, 0.01) and normalise them to sum to 1. Then refit each member on the full training set as now and form total = sum_i w_i * rankdata(p_i) before the existing min-max scaling. Keep the hyperparameters and feature sets unchanged; this costs one extra pass of the three models (six fits per fold total), which should fit the time budget.
backlog.title: Inner out-of-fold weights for the rank average

backlog.spec: Replace the single radius-2 Morgan bit matrix with the horizontal concatenation of 1024-bit count Morgan fingerprints at radius 1 and radius 3 (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Keep the atom-pair and MACCS members and the rank averaging unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-scale Morgan counts radius 1 and 3

backlog.spec: Extend the feature set with a 12-bin histogram of per-atom Gasteiger partial charges. Compute them with AllChem-free rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(m) on each molecule, take the charge values of heavy atoms, clip them to [-0.5, 0.5], and count them into 12 equal-width bins. Also add the total positive and total negative charge sums. Use the result as an extra fourth member, an XGBoost trained on these 14 columns plus the 10 curated descriptors, rank-averaged with the existing members.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge histogram features

backlog.spec: Test whether ExtraTrees is simply the better learner here rather than just a useful extra voice. Keep fingerprints() and the rank-averaging structure of fit_predict exactly as they are, but replace the XGBClassifier inside the loop over feature sets with an ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=800, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, bootstrap=False, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8), so there are three ExtraTrees fits, one each on Morgan presence bits, atom-pair counts and MACCS keys. Rank-transform each member's predict_proba[:, 1] and min-max scale the sum, as now. This is a clean model-family swap inside the proven three-feature-set architecture; report the loss even if it is worse, because a clearly worse result tells us the earlier 0.0866 was noise rather than a real ExtraTrees advantage.
backlog.title: All-ExtraTrees ensemble over the three feature sets

backlog.spec: Keep the architecture exactly as it is, but reduce prediction variance by fitting each of the three per-feature-set XGBoost members with three different seeds instead of one. For each feature set, loop over s in (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000), fit XGBClassifier with the current hyperparameters (n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, random_state=s) and also pass that same s so the subsample/colsample draws differ, average the three class-1 probability vectors, rankdata the average, and add it to `total`. This is nine fits per fold rather than three; verify the job still finishes under 10 minutes (reduce n_estimators to 400 if needed).
backlog.title: Seed averaging of the three XGBoost members

backlog.spec: Re-run the slot-24 configuration unchanged to get a second measurement of its 0.0866 result, which is currently one noise-sized step below the incumbent and never replicated. Keep the incumbent three-feature-set XGBoost rank-average ensemble exactly as it is, and add one more rank-averaged member: a single sklearn ExtraTreesClassifier with n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, fitted on the horizontal concatenation of the three existing feature matrices (Morgan presence bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS keys) built by fingerprints(). Convert its predict_proba[:, 1] with scipy.stats.rankdata and add it to the running total with the same unit weight as each XGBoost member, then min-max scale the total as the current code already does. No other change; the point of this slot is purely a replicate, so do not retune anything.
backlog.title: Replicate the ExtraTrees fourth member

backlog.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged XGBoost member trained on the 10 curated descriptors only, with tree_method='hist', max_bin=16, max_depth=4, n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, min_child_weight=5, random_state=seed. Coarse split thresholds act as a smoothing prior on the continuous physchem features. Give this member the same weight as each of the others in the rank average.
backlog.title: Coarse histogram binning as a regularizer on the descriptor member

backlog.spec: Add a rank-averaged member that is a probability-free SVM: QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=200, output_distribution='normal') then StandardScaler on the 10 curated descriptors, fitted on the training fold only. Use SVC(kernel='rbf', C=1.0, gamma='scale') and take decision_function on the test fold as the score, which is rank-averaged with the other members, so no Platt scaling is needed. Keep the three XGBoost members unchanged.
backlog.title: RBF SVC on quantile-scaled curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the XGBoost member on each of the three feature sets with an ExtraTreesClassifier, keeping the ensemble structure identical. For each of the three feature matrices (Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS) fit ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=1000, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, bootstrap=False, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8), take the class-1 probability, rankdata it and sum across the three members, then min-max scale as now. This tests whether the earlier ExtraTrees gain came from the model family rather than from pooling features, and it removes all XGBoost hyperparameters from the script.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees on each feature set instead of XGBoost

backlog.spec: Add a fourth XGBoost member (same hyperparameters as the others) on 2048-bit topological torsion count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048). Include it in the rank average with equal weight.
backlog.title: Topological torsion fingerprint member

backlog.spec: Reduce the run-to-run variance of the incumbent rather than change its structure. Wrap the existing body of fit_predict in a loop over three sub-seeds derived from the seed argument (for example seed, seed+1000, seed+2000). For each sub-seed, build the three XGBoost members exactly as now (same hyperparameters, random_state set to the sub-seed) and accumulate the rank-transformed test probabilities of all nine resulting fits into one running total, then min-max scale the total once at the end. Do not change the feature sets or hyperparameters. Keep n_jobs at 8 and check the runtime: the incumbent job is well under the limit, but nine XGBoost fits per fold must still finish inside 10 minutes for all 15 fits; if it does not, cut to two sub-seeds.
backlog.title: Seed-average the whole ensemble three times

backlog.spec: Keep the three per-feature-set XGBoost members. Add two members: an ExtraTreesClassifier (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 2) on concatenated features, and a random-subspace XGBoost bag of 12 small models (200 rounds, depth 4, colsample_bytree 0.15) on the concatenated features, each with a different seed. Rank-average all five members equally.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees plus random-subspace XGBoost combined

backlog.spec: Several single extra members each landed slightly below the incumbent but within noise (ErG 0.0884, Gobbi pharmacophore 0.0880, Avalon counts 0.0885). Add all three at once so their independent gains can accumulate. Extend fingerprints() to return six matrices: the current Morgan bits, atom-pair counts and MACCS, plus (a) rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(m), (b) the Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprint folded to 2048 bits via Generate.Gen2DFingerprint with Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory and numpy conversion, and (c) pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP(m, nBits=1024) converted to a dense array. Fit the same XGBClassifier configuration on each of the six matrices, rankdata each class-1 probability and sum all six before the min-max scaling. Wrap each new featurizer in a try/except that falls back to a zero row for molecules that fail.
backlog.title: Three extra fingerprint members added together

backlog.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member that is a logistic regression on the 10 curated descriptors. Build the features with sklearn SplineTransformer (n_knots=5, degree=3, extrapolation='constant') fitted on the training fold only, followed by StandardScaler. Fit LogisticRegression(C=0.5, max_iter=2000, random_state=seed). Its test probabilities go into the same rank average as the three XGBoost members, weighted equally. This gives a smooth, additive, GAM-like physchem model that the tree ensemble cannot express.
backlog.title: Spline-expanded logistic regression on curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Let the data choose how many boosting rounds each member needs instead of fixing 500. Inside fit_predict, split off a stratified 15% inner validation set from the training molecules (random_state=seed). For each of the three feature sets, fit an XGBClassifier with n_estimators=2000 and the incumbent remaining hyperparameters, passing early_stopping_rounds=50 and eval_metric='auc' with the inner validation set as eval_set; note that the installed XGBoost rejects callbacks in fit(), so pass early_stopping_rounds through the constructor if fit() rejects it too. Record the chosen best_iteration, then refit that member on the full training set with n_estimators set to the best iteration scaled up by 1/0.85 (rounded) and predict the test set. Rank-average the three refits and min-max scale as now.
backlog.title: Inner-holdout early stopping for the boosting round count

backlog.spec: In fingerprints(), build the Morgan generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, includeChirality=True) instead of the current default, and keep the count-free presence bits. Stereo-specific environments then become distinct bits. Leave the atom-pair and MACCS sets unchanged, and keep the three-member XGBoost ensemble structure as it is.
backlog.title: Chirality-aware Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Train each XGBoost member as an XGBRegressor with objective reg:logistic on soft targets 0.05 for class 0 and 0.95 for class 1, with otherwise identical hyperparameters. Use predict as the score for rank averaging.
backlog.title: Label smoothing for XGBoost targets

backlog.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member to the existing three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble: an ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8) trained on the horizontal concatenation of the three existing feature matrices (Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS). To cut variance, fit it three times with random_state = seed, seed+1, seed+2, average the three predict_proba class-1 columns, then rankdata that average and add it to `total` exactly like the other members (so total is the sum of four rank vectors before min-max scaling). Keep everything else unchanged. This both replicates the earlier single-seed ExtraTrees result (0.0866) and reduces its run-to-run noise; it should stay well inside the 10-minute budget.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged ExtraTrees fourth member

backlog.spec: Regularise the three XGBoost members with input-level augmentation instead of changing hyperparameters. For each feature set, build an augmented training matrix by stacking the original rows plus two corrupted copies: in each copy, independently zero out each nonzero entry with probability 0.15 using a numpy default_rng seeded with seed, keeping the labels unchanged (so the training set is 3x larger). Fit the existing XGBClassifier configuration on the augmented matrix, but lower n_estimators to 400 to keep runtime in budget, and predict on the untouched test matrix. Rank-average the three members as now. This teaches each model not to rely on any single substructure bit, which should help on folds of unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Bit-dropout augmentation of the training rows

memo:
Helped: curated 10-feature descriptors (0.1243 vs 0.1361 start). Ensembling three models on different feature sets gave the biggest gain (0.1002). XGBoost in that ensemble gave 0.0934 and 0.0879 (incumbent mean 0.0906).

Did not help: single-model swaps (CatBoost 0.1264, Tanimoto SVC 0.1255, logistic regression 0.1264, LightGBM 0.0979). Also no help: one RF on combined features (0.1011), strong regularization (0.1058), scaffold bagging (0.0995), scaffold weighting (0.0977), self-training (0.0920), count Morgan (0.0912), feature filtering (0.0940), auxiliary regressors (0.0942), naive Bayes (0.0947), GP (0.0926).

Fourth-member additions sit near noise (sd about 0.0049). Best singles: ExtraTrees 0.0866, random-subspace XGBoost 0.0873, Gobbi 0.0880, ErG 0.0884. None replicated.

Next: replicate ExtraTrees and random-subspace first. Then try them together. Accept only if the replicate is below 0.088. Stop small tweaks and new featurizers.
